h: פָּרָשַׁת כִּי תָבוֹא, ז׳ Ki Savo, 7
Bikkurim Reveal Divine Unity Within the Lowest Earthly Places

p: Behold, Shabbos is not a time for tefillin,
is in its very essence the sign of tefillin.
And one may say regarding this:
Behold, it is brought in the Tikkunim
that the leather of the tefillin
the leather of the tefillin of the head
corresponds to the holiness of the Name Ehekeh,
נֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת שֵׁם הוי״ה בָּרוּךְ הוּא
correspond to the holiness of the Name Havayah, blessed be He,
and the tefillin of the arm
correspond to the holiness of the Name Adnus.
And the holiness of the three meals of Shabbos
לִקְדוּשַּׁת שְׁלֹשֶׁת הַשֵּׁמוֹת הַקְּדוֹשִׁים הַנִּזְכָּרִים לְעֵיל
to the holiness of the three holy Names mentioned above,
And through the illumination of the holiness of Shabbos
"In the Torah scroll of Rabbi Meir
That is, a person refines himself
and draws down upon himself the light
of His holiness, may He be blessed;
and as it is brought in the Midrash (Bamidbar Rabbah 4:8)
garments of skin, and He clothed them" (Bereishis 3:21):
that in the matter of bikkurim too
to the unification of these three holy Names,
in understanding what is this new matter
that he says to the Kohen
"that I have come to the land
which Hashem swore to our forefathers."
And also the wording that he says to the Kohen,
"I declare, etc., to Hashem your God":
just as it says in this parshah
where it refers to the Kohen?
that the essential beginning of our holiness
began with Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
and he called His Name, may He be blessed,
that even in every kind of earthiness,
the providence of Hashem, may He be blessed, is found,
and there is no place at all empty
of His providence, may He be blessed.
וְלָכֵן הִדְבִּיק אֵלָיו גַּם אֶת לוֹט
Therefore he attached even Lot to himself,
the root of the kingship of the House of David,
which was to come forth from him;
and he risked his life for him
And after this he stood astonished,
that nothing would remain after him;
to implant the holiness of Hashem, may He be blessed,
in the earth for all generations.
although he would draw and give others to drink
from the Torah of his master,
he had no satisfaction from him.
Only when it was said to him,
כִּי אִם אֲשֶׁר יֵצֵא מִמֵּעֶיךָ (שָׁם טו, ד)
but one who shall come forth from your innards" (ibid. 15:4),
does it say, "And he believed in Hashem" (ibid. 15:6);
for in this he was firm
in his faith in Him, may He be blessed,
that he would have holy offspring.
אֲבָל כַּאֲשֶׁר הִבְטִיחַ לוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
But when Hashem, may He be blessed, promised him
that is, that even if a person should be,
sunk in the lowest depths of earthiness,
even from there he would be able to return,
so that there should shine upon him
His providence, may His Name be blessed
בַּמָּה אֵדַע כִּי אִירָשֶׁנָּה (שָׁם טו, ח)
"Whereby shall I know that I shall inherit it?" (ibid. 15:8).
therefore he asked, "Whereby shall I know"
there would be knowledge and recognition for the generations
even in the lowliness of earthiness.
And in reply it was said to him,
קְחָה לִי עֶגְלָה מְשׁוּלֶּשֶׁת (שָׁם טו, ט)
וְנֶאֱמַר וְהִנֵּה אֵימָה חֲשֵׁיכָה וְגוֹמֵר (שָׁם טו, יב)
and it says, "And behold, a dread, a darkness, etc." (ibid. 15:12),
as referring to the four kingdoms.
That is, through the refining and purifying
they would merit the inheritance of the land
that is, to recognizing the aspect of the Kingship of Heaven

that all the days of a person's fleeting life
and when the profit comes to fruition
from the work of his hands,
he can say in his heart
that his strength and the might of his hand

in the vanities of this world,
and the providence of Hashem, may He be blessed,
is forgotten from his heart, Heaven forfend.
וְעַל זֶה בָּא מִצְוַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ

of the fruit of the ground

this was the main earning of wealth

at the very height of immersion in earthiness,
and to go with the first of his fruits
and there he says this declaration to the Kohen:
"I declare today to Hashem your God
that I have come to the land
אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּע ה׳ לַאֲבוֹתֵינוּ (שָׁם כו, ג)
which Hashem swore to our forefathers" (ibid. 26:3).
I have come to the ultimate purpose
of the inheritance of the land:
the providence of Hashem, may He be blessed,
which is at the bottom of the scale,
and not to remain sunk in it,
the ultimate unity of the aspect of "Echad"
that is, that the providence of Hashem, may He be blessed,
for to this the word "Echad" alludes:
of the three holy Names mentioned above.
the aspect of the supernal Wonder,
alludes to the Name Havayah, blessed be He,
which corresponds to the eight holy sefiros
that mediate from the attribute of Atika
down to the attribute of Malchus,
corresponds to the holy Name Adnus,
the attribute of Malchus, the receiver;
the final hei of the Name Havayah,
as it is brought in the holy Zohar:
עַד דְּלָא קַבִּילַת דְּכַר (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קעח, ב)
until it received the male" (Zohar II 178b).

in what is said in this parshah

through which we have a bond

And the pasuk "I declare today to Hashem your God,"
which he says to the Kohen,
כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א רלד, ב)
as it is brought in the holy Zohar (Zohar I 234b)
that "haggadah" is the secret of wisdom
that is, the aspect of the supernal Wonder,
And this is why he says it in the language "to Hashem your God":
for only the Kohen has a grasp
the grasp of the ordinary Yisrael.
"that I have come to the land."
the aspect of the attribute of Malchus,

from the loftiest heights down to the earth,

through the bringing of the bikkurim,

'An Aramean sought to destroy my father,

since we do not find anything like this,
to recall the kindnesses of the Omnipresent, blessed be He,
specifically that he was saved from Lavan;
it would have been greater praise to recall
that he was saved from the hand of Esav,

was in the aspect of truth,
And it is known that the main dominion
of the power of the nations over Yisrael
is when there is a claim against Yisrael
in order to purify them in this trait.
וְהִנֵּה עַל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
Now against Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
there could be, on the surface,
that there was in him something
contrary to the aspect of his holiness,
for on the surface his conduct
the opposite of the aspect of truth.
And this was the power of Lavan the Aramean,
as it is brought in the Midrash (Bereishis Rabbah 75:5)
that he was the master of tricksters.
Therefore he is called here specifically
because through his power in this
against Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him.
